definition_zh: 矛盾的；相互抵触的；爱反驳的
definition_en: involving, containing, or causing a contradiction; expressing opposite ideas; given to contradicting others
core_image: 两个箭头指向相反方向，彼此顶撞
scene: The two witnesses gave contradictory accounts of what happened.
sceneCN: 这里 contradictory 是「矛盾的」（第 1 个义项：包含矛盾的）；句意：两位目击者对所发生的事给出了相互矛盾的描述。图中可辨识物件：两个人、两个相反的箭头、法庭、证词。

senses.title: Involving a contradiction
senses.definition: containing or involving two statements that cannot both be true
senses.definitionCN: 包含两个不能同时为真的陈述的
senses.example: His explanation was contradictory and confusing.
senses.exampleCN: 他的解释自相矛盾，令人困惑。
senses.why: Latin dicere 'to say' + contra 'against': contradictory is 'said against', i.e., in conflict.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 dicere「说」+ contra「反对」：contradictory 是「对着说」，即冲突。

senses.title: Mutually opposed
senses.definition: so opposed that both cannot be true or possible at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 如此对立以至于不能同时为真或同时成立
senses.example: The two theories are contradictory.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个理论是相互矛盾的。
senses.why: Two things are contradictory when one asserts what the other denies.
senses.whyCN: 当一个断言另一个所否定的东西时，两者就是 contradictory 的。

senses.title: Given to contradicting others
senses.definition: tending to oppose or disagree with what others say
senses.definitionCN: 倾向于反对或不同意他人所说的
senses.example: He has a contradictory personality and always argues.
senses.exampleCN: 他性格爱唱反调，总要争论。
senses.why: A contradictory person speaks against others habitually.
senses.whyCN: 一个 contradictory 的人习惯性地对着他人说话。

senses.title: Conflicting with reality
senses.definition: conflicting with what is actually the case
senses.definitionCN: 与实际情况冲突的
senses.example: His claims are contradictory to the evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 他的说法与证据相矛盾。
senses.why: Something is contradictory to the facts when it says the opposite of them.
senses.whyCN: 当某物说的与事实相反时，它就与事实 contradictory。

senses.title: Inconsistent within itself
senses.definition: containing parts that disagree with each other
senses.definitionCN: 包含彼此不一致的部分的
senses.example: The report was internally contradictory.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告内部自相矛盾。
senses.why: When a single source contains opposing statements, it is internally contradictory.
senses.whyCN: 当一个来源包含对立陈述时，它就是内部 contradictory 的。

senses.title: In logic, a contradictory proposition
senses.definition: in logic, a proposition that denies exactly what another asserts
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑学中，恰好否定另一命题所断言内容的命题
senses.example: 'Some S is P' and 'No S is P' are contradictories.
senses.exampleCN: 「有些 S 是 P」和「没有 S 是 P」是矛盾命题。
senses.why: In logic, contradictories cannot both be true and cannot both be false.
senses.whyCN: 在逻辑学中，矛盾命题不能同真也不能同假。

senses.title: Impossible to reconcile
senses.definition: so different that they cannot be made compatible
senses.definitionCN: 如此不同以至于无法兼容的
senses.example: The two values are contradictory and cannot both be pursued.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种价值观相互矛盾，无法同时追求。
senses.why: Contradictory values pull in opposite directions and cannot both be satisfied.
senses.whyCN: 矛盾的价值观拉向相反方向，不能同时满足。

senses.title: Disagreeing loudly or habitually
senses.definition: characterized by habitual opposition in speech
senses.definitionCN: 以习惯性言语反对为特征的
senses.example: Her contradictory tone annoyed everyone at the table.
senses.exampleCN: 她动辄反驳的语气惹恼了桌上所有人。
senses.why: This sense stresses the manner of speaking against, not just logical conflict.
senses.whyCN: 此义强调对着说的方式，而不仅是逻辑冲突。

intro.en: Contradictory comes from Late Latin contradictorius, from contradicere 'to speak against'. The root is dicere 'to say', with contra 'against'.
intro.cn: contradictory 来自后期拉丁 contradictorius，源自 contradicere「对着说」。词根是 dicere「说」，前缀 contra「反对」。

items.en: dicere meant 'to say, speak, declare'. It is the root of many English words: dictate, predict, verdict, dictionary.
items.cn: dicere 意为「说、讲、宣告」。它是许多英语词的词根：dictate、predict、verdict、dictionary。

items.en: contra- means 'against'. contradicere is 'to speak against'.
items.cn: contra- 意为「反对」。contradicere 是「对着说」。

items.en: contradictus, past participle of contradicere, gave the stem used in English contradict.
items.cn: contradictus，contradicere 的过去分词，提供了英语 contradict 所用的词干。

items.en: contradictorius meant 'relating to contradiction'. It was borrowed into French and English.
items.cn: contradictorius 意为「与矛盾相关的」。它被借入法语和英语。

items.en: Contradictory entered English in the 15th century, first in logic and rhetoric.
items.cn: contradictory 在 15 世纪进入英语，最初用于逻辑和修辞。

items.en: Today it appears in logic, law, science, and everyday talk about conflict.
items.cn: 如今它出现在逻辑、法律、科学以及关于冲突的日常谈论中。

note.en: The first group shares dicere; the second contains near-synonyms for conflicting.
note.cn: 第一组共享 dicere；第二组是冲突的近义词。

entries.definition: to assert the opposite; the verb behind contradictory
entries.definitionCN: 断言相反；contradictory 背后的动词

entries.definition: a combination of opposite statements; the noun behind contradictory
entries.definitionCN: 相反陈述的组合；contradictory 背后的名词

entries.definition: to say before; pre- 'before' + dicere
entries.definitionCN: 预言；pre-「前」+ dicere

entries.definition: not staying the same throughout; close to contradictory but less absolute
entries.definitionCN: 前后不一致的；接近 contradictory 但不那么绝对

entries.definition: in disagreement or opposition; a more general term than contradictory
entries.definitionCN: 不一致或对立的；比 contradictory 更通用

entries.definition: completely different; contradictory adds the idea that both cannot be true
entries.definitionCN: 完全不同的；contradictory 还包含两者不能同真的含义

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real word relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分和真实同族词。

normal.en: contra- 'against' + dicere 'to say': contradictory is speaking against, in conflict.
normal.cn: contra-「反对」+ dicere「说」：contradictory 是对着说，相冲突。

normal.en: contradict is the verb; contradictory is the adjective describing that conflict.
normal.cn: contradict 是动词；contradictory 是描述该冲突的形容词。

normal.en: predict says before; contradict says against; both use dicere 'to say'.
normal.cn: predict 向前说；contradict 对着说；都用 dicere「说」。

normal.en: self-contradictory means something disagrees with itself.
normal.cn: self-contradictory 意为某物与自己矛盾。

normal.en: In logic, contradictories are pairs that can't both be true or both be false.
normal.cn: 在逻辑中，矛盾命题是不能同真也不能同假的对子。

abstract.en: Think of two arrows pointing at each other and colliding head-on: that's contradictory.
abstract.cn: 想象两支箭对指着迎头相撞：这就是 contradictory。

abstract.en: Think of one person saying 'yes' while another says 'no' about the same thing.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人说「是」而另一个人对同一件事说「否」。

abstract.en: Think of a scale tipping both ways at once — impossible, hence contradictory.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平同时向两边倾斜——不可能，因此是 contradictory。

examples.en: The witness gave contradictory testimony on two different days.
examples.cn: 证人在两天里给出了相互矛盾的证词。

examples.en: These two findings are contradictory and cannot both be correct.
examples.cn: 这两个发现相互矛盾，不可能都正确。

examples.en: His policy is self-contradictory: it promises both higher spending and lower taxes.
examples.cn: 他的政策自相矛盾：既承诺更高支出又承诺更低税收。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「康吹迪克特瑞」——康（con）师傅对着（contra）说（dicere）的人唱反调 → contradictory 矛盾的

root: 拉丁 contradicere「反驳、与……矛盾」（contra-「反对」+ dicere「说」）；contradict- 词干 + -ory 形容词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all mean 'speaking against': statements, theories, personalities, or logical propositions may be contradictory.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都表示「对着说」：陈述、理论、性格或逻辑命题都可能是 contradictory 的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two arrows clashing head-on.
core.cn: 核心意象：两支箭迎头相撞。

branches.en: LOGICAL CONFLICT: statements that cannot both hold.
branches.cn: 逻辑冲突：不能同时成立的陈述。

branches.en: MUTUAL OPPOSITION: things so opposed they cannot coexist.
branches.cn: 相互对立：如此对立以至于不能共存的事物。

branches.en: OPPOSITIONAL PERSON: someone who habitually speaks against.
branches.cn: 唱反调的人：习惯性对着说的人。

branches.en: AGAINST EVIDENCE: claims that clash with the facts.
branches.cn: 违背证据：与事实冲突的主张。

branches.en: LOGICAL CONTRADICTORY: a proposition that is the exact opposite.
branches.cn: 逻辑矛盾命题：恰好相反的命题。

intro.en: Contradictory is the -ory adjective from contradict. The suffix -ory means 'having the nature of'; the inner parts are fossilized.
intro.cn: contradictory 是 contradict 的 -ory 形容词。后缀 -ory 意为「具有……性质的」；内部部分已凝固。

latinIntro.en: Latin dicere 'to say' produced a large family: dictate, predict, contradict, verdict, dictionary, dedicate, indicate. The root appears as dic-, dict-, or dit-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 dicere「说」产生了大家族：dictate、predict、contradict、verdict、dictionary、dedicate、indicate。词根以 dic-、dict- 或 dit- 形式出现。

definition_en: a situation in which two statements, ideas, or facts are opposed and cannot both be true; the act of contradicting
core_image: 两句话背道而驰，无法同时成立
scene: There is a contradiction between what he said yesterday and what he says today.
sceneCN: 这里 contradiction 是「矛盾」（第 1 个义项：两个陈述不能同真）；句意：他昨天说的和今天说的之间存在矛盾。图中可辨识物件：两张纸条、两个相反的箭头、思考的人。

collocations.zh: 用词矛盾（如「正方形的圆」）

senses.title: Two statements that cannot both be true
senses.definition: a combination of statements, ideas, or features that oppose each other and cannot both be true
senses.definitionCN: 相互对立、不能同时为真的陈述、观念或特征的组合
senses.example: His actions are in contradiction to his promises.
senses.exampleCN: 他的行动与他的承诺相矛盾。
senses.why: Latin dicere 'to say' + contra 'against': a contradiction is one thing said against another.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 dicere「说」+ contra「反对」：contradiction 是对着另一事物说的话。

senses.title: The act of contradicting
senses.definition: the act of saying the opposite of what someone else has said
senses.definitionCN: 说与他人所说相反的话的行为
senses.example: Her contradiction of his claim surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 她对他主张的反驳让所有人惊讶。
senses.why: A contradiction can be the event of speaking against, not just the resulting conflict.
senses.whyCN: contradiction 可以是对着说的事件，而不仅是结果的冲突。

senses.title: An inconsistency within something
senses.definition: a lack of agreement between parts of the same thing
senses.definitionCN: 同一事物各部分之间缺乏一致
senses.example: The novel contains a contradiction in its timeline.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说在时间线上存在矛盾。
senses.why: When a single thing disagrees with itself, it contains a contradiction.
senses.whyCN: 当一物与自己不一致时，它就包含 contradiction。

senses.title: A logical impossibility
senses.definition: in logic, a proposition that is necessarily false
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑学中，必然为假的命题
senses.example: 'P and not P' is a contradiction.
senses.exampleCN: 「P 且非 P」是一个矛盾命题。
senses.why: In logic, a contradiction is a statement that cannot be true under any interpretation.
senses.whyCN: 在逻辑学中，contradiction 是在任何解释下都不能为真的陈述。

senses.title: A clash between opposed forces
senses.definition: a direct conflict between opposing principles or forces
senses.definitionCN: 对立原则或力量之间的直接冲突
senses.example: There is a contradiction between freedom and equality in some contexts.
senses.exampleCN: 在某些语境下自由与平等之间存在矛盾。
senses.why: When two values pull in opposite directions, they form a contradiction.
senses.whyCN: 当两种价值观拉向相反方向时，它们就形成 contradiction。

senses.title: A denial or refutation
senses.definition: the act of denying the truth of something
senses.definitionCN: 否认真实性的行为
senses.example: He offered no contradiction to the accusation.
senses.exampleCN: 他对指控未作任何反驳。
senses.why: Here contradiction means a spoken denial of what has been said.
senses.whyCN: 此处 contradiction 意为对所说内容的口头否认。

senses.title: A state of being self-opposed
senses.definition: the condition of containing opposing elements
senses.definitionCN: 包含对立元素的状态
senses.example: The policy is a mass of contradictions.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策充满矛盾。
senses.why: When many opposing elements coexist, the result is a mass of contradictions.
senses.whyCN: 当许多对立元素共存时，结果就是一堆 contradictions。

senses.title: A rhetorical device of contrast
senses.definition: in rhetoric, the juxtaposition of contrasting ideas
senses.definitionCN: 修辞学中，对比观念的并置
senses.example: The poet used contradiction to heighten the effect.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人用对照来加强效果。
senses.why: In rhetoric, contradiction places opposites side by side for effect.
senses.whyCN: 在修辞学中，contradiction 把对立面并置以产生效果。

entries.definition: to say before; pre- + dicere

entries.definition: a serious disagreement; broader than contradiction, which is specifically about opposing claims
entries.definitionCN: 严重分歧；比 contradiction 更广，contradiction 特指对立主张

entries.definition: the quality of not staying the same; close to the internal sense of contradiction

entries.definition: a statement that seems contradictory but may be true; a softer form of contradiction

normal.cn: contra-「反对」+ dicere「说」：contradiction 是一个陈述对着另一个。

normal.cn: contradict 是动词；contradiction 是行为或结果的名词。

normal.en: A 'contradiction in terms' is when the words themselves conflict, like 'a round square'.
normal.cn: 「contradiction in terms」是词语本身冲突，如「圆的方」。

normal.en: self-contradiction is when one's own statements conflict.
normal.cn: self-contradiction 是自己的陈述相互冲突。

normal.en: In logic, a contradiction is always false, like 'it is raining and not raining'.
normal.cn: 在逻辑中，contradiction 永远为假，如「下雨且不下雨」。

abstract.en: Think of two signs: one says 'Open', the other 'Closed', on the same door — a contradiction.
abstract.cn: 想象同一扇门上有两块牌子：一块写「营业中」，另一块写「已关门」——这就是 contradiction。

abstract.en: Think of a sentence that asserts and denies the same thing at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一个句子同时断言和否定同一件事。

abstract.en: Think of two arrows pulling a statement apart — it cannot hold, hence a contradiction.
abstract.cn: 想象两支箭把一个陈述向两边拉——它撑不住，因此是 contradiction。

examples.en: There is a contradiction between the two versions of the story.
examples.cn: 这个故事的两个版本之间存在矛盾。

examples.en: A contradiction in terms is a phrase like 'a silent scream'.
examples.cn: 「用词矛盾」指类似「无声的尖叫」这样的短语。

examples.en: His behavior is full of contradictions he cannot explain.
examples.cn: 他的行为充满了他无法解释的矛盾。

sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都表示「对着说」：陈述之间、事物内部，或作为逻辑不可能。

core.cn: 核心意象：两个陈述向相反方向拉扯。

branches.cn: 对立主张：不能共存的陈述或特征。

branches.en: ACT OF DENIAL: the event of speaking against.
branches.cn: 否认行为：对着说的事件。

branches.en: INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY: a thing disagreeing with itself.
branches.cn: 内部不一致：事物与自己不一致。

branches.en: LOGICAL CONTRADICTION: a necessarily false proposition.
branches.cn: 逻辑矛盾：必然为假的命题。

branches.cn: 冲突或对照：对立力量或修辞对照。

definition_zh: 贡献；捐款；投稿；促成因素
definition_en: something given or done to help achieve a common result; money donated; an article for publication; a factor that helps cause something
core_image: 把自己手里的东西放进共同的篮子里
scene: Her contribution to the project was recognized at the annual meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 contribution 是「贡献」（第 1 个义项：为共同结果所做的付出）；句意：她对项目的贡献在年会上得到了认可。图中可辨识物件：颁奖台、奖杯、项目文件、鼓掌的人。

senses.title: Something given to a common cause
senses.definition: something that you give or do to help produce or achieve something together with others
senses.definitionCN: 你为与他人一起产生或完成某事而给予或做的东西
senses.example: Every contribution, no matter how small, helps.
senses.exampleCN: 每一份贡献，无论多小，都有帮助。
senses.why: Latin tribuere 'to assign, allot' + con-: contribuere means 'to bring together, give a share'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 tribuere「分配、分派」+ con-：contribuere 意为「聚到一起、出一份」。

senses.title: Money given to a fund or charity
senses.definition: a sum of money given to a fund, charity, or organization
senses.definitionCN: 给予基金、慈善机构或组织的一笔钱
senses.example: We received a large contribution from a donor.
senses.exampleCN: 我们收到了一位捐赠者的大额捐款。
senses.why: When you contribute money, your contribution is the amount given.
senses.whyCN: 当你捐钱时，你的 contribution 就是所给的数额。

senses.title: An article submitted for publication
senses.definition: an article or piece of writing submitted to a publication
senses.definitionCN: 投给出版物的文章或作品
senses.example: The magazine accepts contributions from freelance writers.
senses.exampleCN: 该杂志接受自由撰稿人的投稿。
senses.why: A written contribution is a piece 'brought together' for a publication.
senses.whyCN: 书面 contribution 是为出版物「聚到一起」的作品。

senses.title: A factor that helps cause something
senses.definition: something that helps cause or influence a result
senses.definitionCN: 帮助导致或影响结果的东西
senses.example: Poor diet was a major contribution to his illness.
senses.exampleCN: 饮食不良是他患病的主要促成因素。
senses.why: A contributing factor 'brings' its influence to the outcome.
senses.whyCN: 促成因素把它的影响「带到」结果中。

senses.title: A share of the total cost
senses.definition: the part of a cost that a particular person or group pays
senses.definitionCN: 特定个人或团体所支付的那部分费用
senses.example: Employees make a monthly contribution to the pension fund.
senses.exampleCN: 员工每月向养老基金缴纳分摊款。
senses.why: In finance, a contribution is the share one pays toward a common cost.

senses.title: The act of giving or adding
senses.definition: the act of giving something to a common fund or purpose
senses.definitionCN: 把某物给予共同基金或目的的行为
senses.example: His contribution of time was invaluable.
senses.exampleCN: 他付出的时间极为宝贵。
senses.why: Contribution can name the act, not just the thing given.
senses.whyCN: contribution 可以命名行为，而不仅是所给之物。

senses.title: A part played in a result
senses.definition: the role that something plays in producing a result
senses.definitionCN: 某物在产生结果中所起的作用
senses.example: The contribution of genetics to intelligence is debated.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传对智力的作用存在争议。
senses.why: Here contribution means the share of influence a factor has on an outcome.
senses.whyCN: 此处 contribution 意为一因素对结果的影响份额。

senses.title: A tax or levy paid
senses.definition: a payment required by law, such as a tax or social contribution
senses.definitionCN: 法律要求的付款，如税款或社保缴费
senses.example: Self-employed workers pay social contributions.
senses.exampleCN: 自由职业者缴纳社保费。
senses.why: In legal contexts, contributions are mandatory payments to a public fund.
senses.whyCN: 在法律语境中，contributions 是向公共基金的强制性付款。

abstract.en: Think of everyone putting a coin into one pot: each coin is a contribution.
abstract.cn: 想象每个人把一枚硬币放进同一个锅里：每枚硬币就是一份 contribution。

abstract.en: Think of a potluck dinner: each dish is a contribution to the meal.
abstract.cn: 想象每人自带一道菜的聚餐：每道菜就是对这顿饭的 contribution。

abstract.en: Think of a writer sending an article to a magazine: that article is a contribution.
abstract.cn: 想象一位作家给杂志投了一篇文章：那篇文章就是一份 contribution。

examples.en: Her contribution to the field of medicine was widely recognized.

examples.en: The charity relies on voluntary contributions from the public.
examples.cn: 该慈善机构依赖公众的自愿捐款。

examples.en: Stress is a significant contribution to heart disease.

definition_en: a person or thing that contributes something, especially money, articles, or effort; a factor that helps cause something

scene: She is a regular contributor to the magazine's science section.
sceneCN: 这里 contributor 是「投稿人」（第 3 个义项：投稿的人）；句意：她是该杂志科学栏目的常驻投稿人。图中可辨识物件：杂志、信封、打字机、作者。

senses.title: A person who gives something
senses.definition: a person who gives something such as money, time, or ideas to help a common purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为帮助共同目的而给予金钱、时间或想法等东西的人
senses.example: The charity thanked all its contributors.
senses.exampleCN: 慈善机构感谢了所有捐款者。
senses.why: contribuere 'to give a share' + -or 'one who does': a contributor is one who gives a share.
senses.whyCN: contribuere「出一份」+ -or「做……的人」：contributor 是出一份的人。

senses.title: A person who donates money
senses.definition: a person who gives money to a fund, charity, or political campaign
senses.definitionCN: 向基金、慈善机构或政治运动捐钱的人
senses.example: The foundation lists its top contributors each year.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金会每年列出其主要捐款者。
senses.why: When the contribution is money, the contributor is a donor.
senses.whyCN: 当 contribution 是金钱时，contributor 就是捐赠者。

senses.title: A person who writes for publication
senses.definition: a person who submits articles or other writing to a publication
senses.definitionCN: 向出版物投送文章或其他文字的人
senses.example: He is a frequent contributor to this newspaper.
senses.exampleCN: 他是本报的频繁撰稿人。
senses.why: A contributor to a magazine 'brings' written pieces to it.
senses.whyCN: 杂志的 contributor 把书面作品「带来」给它。

senses.title: A factor that helps cause an outcome
senses.definition: something that helps cause or influence a result
senses.definitionCN: 帮助导致或影响结果的事物
senses.example: Smoking is a major contributor to lung cancer.
senses.exampleCN: 吸烟是肺癌的主要促成因素。
senses.why: By extension, a non-person that 'brings' an influence is also a contributor.
senses.whyCN: 引申而言，「带来」影响的非人物也可以是 contributor。

senses.title: A person who pays into a fund
senses.definition: a person who makes regular payments into a pension or insurance fund
senses.definitionCN: 定期向养老或保险基金付款的人
senses.example: All contributors to the plan receive annual statements.
senses.exampleCN: 该计划的所有出资人每年都收到对账单。
senses.why: In finance, contributors are those who pay into a shared fund.
senses.whyCN: 在财务中，contributors 是向共同基金付款的人。

senses.title: A participant in a project
senses.definition: a person who takes part in and helps with a project or activity
senses.definitionCN: 参与并帮助项目或活动的人
senses.example: She was a contributor to the research paper.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这篇研究论文的参与者。
senses.why: Anyone who adds work to a project is a contributor.
senses.whyCN: 任何为项目添砖加瓦的人都是 contributor。

senses.title: A contributing cause or source
senses.definition: a cause or source that adds to a particular result
senses.definitionCN: 添加到特定结果中的原因或来源
senses.example: Stress is a known contributor to high blood pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 压力是已知的高血压成因之一。
senses.why: This sense treats the cause as something that 'contributes' to the outcome.
senses.whyCN: 此义把原因当作对结果「作出贡献」的东西。

senses.title: A writer listed by a publication
senses.definition: a writer whose work appears in a publication, often listed by name
senses.definitionCN: 作品出现在出版物中、常被列明姓名的作者
senses.example: The issue features contributors from three continents.
senses.exampleCN: 这期杂志有来自三大洲的作者。
senses.why: In publishing, contributors are the named writers of pieces.
senses.whyCN: 在出版业中，contributors 是作品署名的作者。

definition_en: in a way that follows accepted customs, traditions, or usual practices
core_image: 大家都走同一条老路，没人偏离
scene: Conventionally, the bride wears white at a Western wedding.
sceneCN: 这里 conventionally 是「按惯例」（第 1 个义项：遵循传统习俗）；句意：按惯例，西方婚礼上新娘穿白色。图中可辨识物件：新娘、白纱、教堂、宾客。

senses.title: According to accepted custom
senses.definition: in accordance with accepted customs or traditions
senses.definitionCN: 依照公认的习俗或传统
senses.example: Conventionally, the eldest son inherits the family business.
senses.exampleCN: 按惯例，长子继承家族企业。
senses.why: Latin convenire 'to come together': a convention is what people agree on when they come together; conventionally follows that agreement.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 convenire「聚到一起」：convention 是人们聚在一起时达成的共识；conventionally 遵循该共识。

senses.title: In the usual or ordinary way
senses.definition: in the usual, ordinary, or standard way
senses.definitionCN: 以通常、普通或标准的方式
senses.example: The engine is conventionally powered by gasoline.
senses.exampleCN: 该发动机以常规方式由汽油驱动。
senses.why: When something is done conventionally, it follows the standard practice, not an innovation.
senses.whyCN: 当某事 conventionally 完成时，它遵循标准做法，而非创新。

senses.title: By general agreement
senses.definition: as generally agreed or commonly accepted
senses.definitionCN: 如一般所同意或普遍接受的
senses.example: The term is conventionally used to mean 'very large'.
senses.exampleCN: 这个术语按惯例用来表示「非常大」。
senses.why: Here conventionally means 'by the shared convention of the speech community'.
senses.whyCN: 此处 conventionally 意为「按言语社区的共同约定」。

senses.title: In a non-nuclear way
senses.definition: using ordinary weapons rather than nuclear ones
senses.definitionCN: 使用常规武器而非核武器
senses.example: The country relies on conventionally armed forces.
senses.exampleCN: 该国依赖常规武装部队。
senses.why: In military terms, conventional means non-nuclear; conventionally modifies the arming.
senses.whyCN: 在军事术语中，conventional 意为非核的；conventionally 修饰武装方式。

senses.title: Without special treatment
senses.definition: without special or alternative methods
senses.definitionCN: 不使用特殊或替代方法
senses.example: The crop was conventionally grown without pesticides.
senses.exampleCN: 该作物以传统方式种植，未使用杀虫剂。
senses.why: Conventionally here means 'by ordinary farming methods', often contrasted with organic.
senses.whyCN: 此处 conventionally 意为「以普通耕作方法」，常与有机种植对比。

senses.title: According to established rules
senses.definition: in a way that follows established rules or procedures
senses.definitionCN: 以遵循既定规则或程序的方式
senses.example: The case was handled conventionally through the courts.
senses.exampleCN: 该案通过法院按常规程序处理。
senses.why: Conventional procedures are those established by long use.
senses.whyCN: 常规程序是经长期使用确立的程序。

senses.title: In a socially accepted manner
senses.definition: in a way that is socially accepted or expected
senses.definitionCN: 以社会接受或期望的方式
senses.example: She behaved conventionally at the formal dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 她在正式晚宴上举止合乎常规。
senses.why: Social conventions dictate what is conventionally acceptable.
senses.whyCN: 社会惯例规定了什么是 conventionally 可接受的。

senses.title: In the traditional sense
senses.definition: in the traditional or established meaning of a term
senses.definitionCN: 在术语的传统或既定意义上
senses.example: Conventionally, a novel is a long prose fiction.
senses.exampleCN: 按传统定义，小说是长篇散文虚构作品。
senses.why: When a word is used conventionally, it has its usual accepted meaning.
senses.whyCN: 当一个词 conventionally 使用时，它具有通常被接受的意义。

intro.en: Conventionally is conventional + -ly. Conventional comes from Latin convention, from convenire 'to come together' (con- + venire). A convention is an agreement people come together on.
intro.cn: conventionally 是 conventional + -ly。conventional 来自拉丁 conventio，conventio 源自 convenire「聚到一起」（con- + venire）。convention 是人们聚在一起达成的协议。

items.en: venire meant 'to come'. convenire is con- 'together' + venire, meaning 'to come together, meet, agree'.
items.cn: venire 意为「来」。convenire 是 con-「一起」+ venire，意为「聚到一起、会面、同意」。

items.en: conventio meant 'a meeting, agreement, convention'. It was borrowed into French and English.
items.cn: conventio 意为「会议、协议、惯例」。它被借入法语和英语。

items.en: Conventional appeared in English in the 15th century, meaning 'arising from a convention or agreement'.
items.cn: conventional 在 15 世纪出现在英语中，意为「源于惯例或协议的」。

items.en: The suffix -ly turns the adjective into an adverb of manner.
items.cn: 后缀 -ly 把形容词变成方式副词。

items.en: conventionally = conventional + -ly, meaning 'in a conventional manner'.
items.cn: conventionally = conventional + -ly，意为「以常规的方式」。

items.en: The word is used in social, military, agricultural, and academic contexts.
items.cn: 该词用于社会、军事、农业和学术语境。

note.en: The first group shares venire; the second contains near-synonymous adverbs.
note.cn: 第一组共享 venire；第二组是近义副词。

entries.definition: following accepted customs; the adjective behind conventionally
entries.definitionCN: 遵循公认习俗的；conventionally 背后的形容词

entries.definition: an accepted custom or a meeting; from convenire
entries.definitionCN: 公认的习俗或会议；来自 convenire

entries.definition: not following accepted customs; un- + conventional
entries.definitionCN: 不遵循公认习俗的；un- + conventional

entries.definition: according to tradition; close to conventionally but stresses handed-down practice
entries.definitionCN: 依照传统；接近 conventionally 但强调传承的做法

entries.definition: in the usual way; broader than conventionally, which stresses custom
entries.definitionCN: 以通常方式；比 conventionally 更广，conventionally 强调习俗

entries.definition: in a standard way; close to the 'usual practice' sense
entries.definitionCN: 以标准方式；接近「通常做法」义

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real word relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分和真实同族词。

normal.en: convenire 'to come together': a convention is what people agree on together; conventionally follows it.
normal.cn: convenire「聚到一起」：convention 是人们共同同意的东西；conventionally 遵循它。

normal.en: conventional is the adjective; conventionally adds -ly for manner.
normal.cn: conventional 是形容词；conventionally 加 -ly 表方式。

normal.en: unconventional is the opposite: not following the convention.
normal.cn: unconventional 是反义词：不遵循惯例。

normal.en: 'Conventionally grown' food is grown the usual way, not organic.
normal.cn: 「传统种植的」食物是以通常方式种植的，不是有机的。

normal.en: 'Conventionally armed' means non-nuclear weapons.
normal.cn: 「常规武装」意为非核武器。

abstract.en: Think of everyone on a road driving on the same side by agreement: that's conventionally.
abstract.cn: 想象路上所有人按约定靠同一侧行驶：这就是 conventionally。

abstract.en: Think of the suffix -ly as 'in the manner of': conventionally = in the manner of conventional.
abstract.cn: 把 -ly 想成「以……的方式」：conventionally = 以 conventional 的方式。

abstract.en: Think of a wedding following all the old customs: done conventionally.
abstract.cn: 想象一场遵循所有旧习俗的婚礼：conventionally 完成。

examples.en: Conventionally, a handshake is a sign of agreement in many cultures.
examples.cn: 按惯例，在许多文化中握手是同意的标志。

examples.en: Conventionally produced food may contain pesticide residues.
examples.cn: 传统方式生产的食品可能含有农药残留。

examples.en: The country's forces are conventionally armed, without nuclear weapons.
examples.cn: 该国部队为常规武装，没有核武器。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「康温神厄里」——康（con）师傅温（venire）柔地走来（-ly），照着老规矩 → conventionally 按惯例

root: 拉丁 convenire「聚到一起、同意」（con-「一起」+ venire「来」）→ conventio 名词 → conventional + -ly 副词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all mean 'in the way people have agreed on': customs, standard practices, social rules, or accepted meanings.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都表示「以人们同意的方式」：习俗、标准做法、社会规则或公认含义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: people walking together on a well-worn path.
core.cn: 核心意象：人们一起走在一条踩熟的路上。

branches.en: SOCIAL CUSTOM: following what people have agreed on.
branches.cn: 社会习俗：遵循人们约定的做法。

branches.en: STANDARD METHOD: using the usual, non-special way.
branches.cn: 标准方法：使用通常的、非特殊的方式。

branches.en: ACCEPTED USAGE: by general agreement of meaning.
branches.cn: 公认用法：按意义的一般共识。

branches.en: NON-NUCLEAR: using ordinary, not nuclear, weapons.
branches.cn: 非核的：使用常规而非核武器。

branches.en: ESTABLISHED PROCEDURE: following the standard rules.
branches.cn: 既定程序：遵循标准规则。

intro.en: Conventionally is conventional + -ly. The suffix -ly is productive; the inner parts are fossilized.
intro.cn: conventionally 是 conventional + -ly。后缀 -ly 有能产性；内部部分已凝固。

latinIntro.en: Latin venire 'to come' produced convene, convention, intervene, prevent, advent, venue. Root: ven-/vent-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 venire「来」产生了 convene、convention、intervene、prevent、advent、venue。词根：ven-/vent-。

definition_zh: 转换；转化；皈依；换算；（橄榄球）触地后附加射门
definition_en: the process of changing something from one form, use, or system to another; a change of religion; the act of scoring extra points after a try in rugby
core_image: 一样东西从一种形态变成另一种形态
scene: The conversion of the old factory into apartments took two years.
sceneCN: 这里 conversion 是「改造」（第 1 个义项：从一种用途改为另一种）；句意：把旧工厂改造成公寓花了两年。图中可辨识物件：旧工厂、公寓楼、起重机、工人。

senses.title: Changing from one form to another
senses.definition: the process of changing something from one form, type, or use to another
senses.definitionCN: 把某物从一种形式、类型或用途变为另一种的过程
senses.example: The conversion of sunlight into electricity is solar power.
senses.exampleCN: 把阳光转化为电力就是太阳能发电。
senses.why: Latin vertere 'to turn' + con-: convertere means 'to turn around, change'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 vertere「转」+ con-：convertere 意为「转身、改变」。

senses.title: A change of religion or belief
senses.definition: a change from one religion or belief to another
senses.definitionCN: 从一种宗教或信仰变为另一种的过程
senses.example: His conversion to Buddhism changed his life.
senses.exampleCN: 他皈依佛教改变了他的生活。
senses.why: When people convert, their beliefs 'turn around' to a new faith.
senses.whyCN: 当人们皈依时，他们的信仰「转身」投向新的宗教。

senses.title: A change of opinion or position
senses.definition: a change in one's opinion, attitude, or position
senses.definitionCN: 一个人观点、态度或立场的改变
senses.example: Her conversion to the cause surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这一事业的支持让所有人惊讶。
senses.why: A conversion of opinion is a turning from one view to another.
senses.whyCN: 观点的 conversion 是从一种看法转向另一种。

senses.title: The act of changing units
senses.definition: the act of changing one unit of measurement into another
senses.definitionCN: 把一种计量单位变为另一种的行为
senses.example: The conversion of miles to kilometers is straightforward.
senses.exampleCN: 英里换算成公里很简单。
senses.why: In math, conversion turns one measure into an equivalent one.
senses.whyCN: 在数学中，conversion 把一种度量变为等价的另一种。

senses.title: Changing property or money
senses.definition: the act of changing property or money into a different form
senses.definitionCN: 把财产或货币变为不同形式的行为
senses.example: The conversion of stocks to cash was quick.
senses.exampleCN: 股票兑换成现金很快。
senses.why: Financial conversion turns one asset into another form.
senses.whyCN: 财务 conversion 把一种资产变为另一种形式。

senses.title: In rugby, an extra score
senses.definition: in rugby, the scoring of extra points by kicking the ball over the bar after a try
senses.definitionCN: 橄榄球中，触地得分后把球踢过横梁而获得额外分数
senses.example: He scored the conversion to tie the game.
senses.exampleCN: 他踢进附加球扳平了比分。
senses.why: In rugby, a try is 'converted' into extra points by a successful kick.
senses.whyCN: 在橄榄球中，触地得分通过成功射门「转化」为额外分数。

senses.title: A change in function or purpose
senses.definition: the process of changing the function or purpose of something
senses.definitionCN: 改变某物功能或用途的过程
senses.example: The conversion of the barn into a theater was successful.
senses.exampleCN: 把谷仓改造成剧院很成功。
senses.why: When a building's use changes, it undergoes conversion.
senses.whyCN: 当一栋建筑的用途改变时，它就经历了 conversion。

senses.title: A change in computer data
senses.definition: the process of changing data from one format to another
senses.definitionCN: 把数据从一种格式变为另一种的过程
senses.example: The file conversion took several minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 文件转换花了几分钟。
senses.why: In computing, data is converted from one format to another for compatibility.
senses.whyCN: 在计算中，数据从一种格式转换为另一种以实现兼容。

intro.en: Conversion comes from Latin conversio, from convertere 'to turn around' (con- + vertere). The core image is turning something into another form.
intro.cn: conversion 来自拉丁 conversio，源自 convertere「转身」（con- + vertere）。核心意象是把某物变为另一种形式。

items.en: vertere meant 'to turn'. It is one of the most productive Latin roots in English.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转」。它是英语中能产性最高的拉丁词根之一。

items.en: con- adds 'together' or intensifies. convertere is 'to turn around, change'.
items.cn: con- 加上「一起」或加强语气。convertere 是「转身、改变」。

items.en: conversus, past participle of convertere, gave the stem used in English convert.
items.cn: conversus，convertere 的过去分词，提供了英语 convert 所用的词干。

items.en: conversio meant 'a turning around, change'. It was borrowed into French and English.
items.cn: conversio 意为「转身、改变」。它被借入法语和英语。

items.en: Conversion entered English in the 13th century from French conversion.
items.cn: conversion 在 13 世纪从法语 conversion 进入英语。

items.en: The word grew to cover religion, finance, computing, and sports.
items.cn: 该词扩展到宗教、金融、计算和体育领域。

note.en: The first group shares vertere; the second contains near-synonyms for change.
note.cn: 第一组共享 vertere；第二组是变化的近义词。

entries.definition: to change from one form to another; the verb behind conversion
entries.definitionCN: 从一种形式变为另一种；conversion 背后的动词

entries.definition: able to be converted; from convert + -ible
entries.definitionCN: 可转换的；来自 convert + -ible

entries.definition: to turn back; re- + vertere
entries.definitionCN: 逆转；re- + vertere

entries.definition: a thorough change in form or appearance; close to conversion
entries.definitionCN: 形式或外观的彻底改变；接近 conversion

entries.definition: the act of becoming different; broader than conversion
entries.definitionCN: 变得不同的行为；比 conversion 更广

entries.definition: the process of changing to suit new conditions; close to the 'change of use' sense
entries.definitionCN: 改变以适应新条件的过程；接近「用途改变」义

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real word relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分和真实同族词。

normal.en: con- + vertere 'to turn': conversion is turning something into another form.
normal.cn: con- + vertere「转」：conversion 是把某物变成另一种形式。

normal.en: convert is the verb; conversion is the noun of the action or result.
normal.cn: convert 是动词；conversion 是动作或结果的名词。

normal.en: reverse (re-) turns back; convert (con-) turns around into something else.
normal.cn: reverse（re-）转回；convert（con-）转身变成别的东西。

normal.en: Religious conversion is a 'turning around' of one's beliefs.

normal.en: In rugby, a try is converted into extra points by a kick.
normal.cn: 在橄榄球中，触地得分通过射门转化为额外分数。

abstract.en: Think of a caterpillar turning into a butterfly: that is conversion of form.
abstract.cn: 想象毛毛虫变成蝴蝶：那是形式的 conversion。

abstract.en: Think of a U-turn: the direction turns around — conversion.
abstract.cn: 想象一个掉头：方向转了过来——conversion。

abstract.en: Think of one currency being changed into another: a financial conversion.
abstract.cn: 想象一种货币换成另一种：财务 conversion。

examples.en: The conversion of the warehouse into offices was completed last month.
examples.cn: 仓库改造成办公室的工程上个月完工了。

examples.en: His conversion to vegetarianism surprised his family.
examples.cn: 他皈依素食主义让家人惊讶。

examples.en: The conversion rate from euros to dollars has changed.
examples.cn: 欧元兑美元的汇率变了。

root: 拉丁 convertere「转身、改变」（con-「一起」+ vertere「转」）；convers- 词干 + -ion 名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all mean 'turning into something else': form, religion, money, units, data, or sports points.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都表示「变成别的东西」：形式、宗教、金钱、单位、数据或体育分数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shape rotating until it becomes another shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个形状旋转直到变成另一个形状。

branches.en: FORM OR USE CHANGE: one thing becomes another kind.
branches.cn: 形式或用途改变：一物变成另一种。

branches.en: BELIEF OR VIEW CHANGE: a turning of opinion or faith.
branches.cn: 信仰或观点改变：意见或信念的转向。

branches.en: MEASURE OR ASSET CHANGE: units or money are turned into equivalents.
branches.cn: 度量或资产改变：单位或货币变为等价物。

branches.en: DATA FORMAT CHANGE: information is turned into another format.
branches.cn: 数据格式改变：信息变为另一种格式。

branches.en: SPORTS CONVERSION: a try is turned into extra points.
branches.cn: 体育得分：触地得分转化为额外分数。

intro.en: Conversion is the Latin-stem noun from convertere. The suffix -ion marks the action; the inner parts are fossilized.
intro.cn: conversion 是来自 convertere 的拉丁词干名词。后缀 -ion 标记动作；内部部分已凝固。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere 'to turn' produced convert, reverse, divert, invert, revert, convert, vertex, version, vortex. Root: vert-/vers-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vertere「转」产生了 convert、reverse、divert、invert、revert、vertex、version、vortex。词根：vert-/vers-。

definition_en: a connection or relationship between two or more things, especially one where one changes as the other changes
core_image: 两条线一起起伏，步调呼应
scene: The study found a strong correlation between exercise and mental health.
sceneCN: 这里 correlation 是「关联」（第 1 个义项：两事物之间的联系）；句意：研究发现运动与心理健康之间存在强关联。图中可辨识物件：坐标图、两条同步起伏的曲线、放大镜。

senses.title: A connection between two things
senses.definition: a connection or relationship between two or more things
senses.definitionCN: 两个或更多事物之间的联系或关系
senses.example: There is a correlation between smoking and lung cancer.
senses.exampleCN: 吸烟与肺癌之间存在关联。
senses.why: Latin referre 'to carry back' → relatio 'relation' + cor- (com-): correlation is a 'together relation'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 referre「带回」→ relatio「关系」+ cor-（com-）：correlation 是「一起的关系」。

senses.title: A measure of how things vary together
senses.definition: in statistics, a measure of the extent to which two variables change together
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中，两个变量一起变化程度的度量
senses.example: The correlation between height and weight is high.
senses.exampleCN: 身高和体重之间的相关度很高。
senses.why: In statistics, correlation quantifies how closely two sets of data move together.
senses.whyCN: 在统计学中，correlation 量化两组数据一起变动的紧密程度。

senses.title: A mutual relationship
senses.definition: a relationship in which two things affect each other
senses.definitionCN: 两事物相互影响的关系
senses.example: The correlation between stress and illness is complex.
senses.exampleCN: 压力与疾病之间的相互关系很复杂。
senses.why: When two things are correlated, they vary in a related way, though one may not cause the other.
senses.whyCN: 当两事物相关时，它们以相关的方式变化，尽管不一定有因果关系。

senses.title: A correspondence between sets
senses.definition: a matching or correspondence between elements of different sets
senses.definitionCN: 不同集合元素之间的匹配或对应
senses.example: There is a correlation between income and education level.
senses.exampleCN: 收入与教育水平之间存在对应关系。
senses.why: Correlation here means the two groups tend to match or correspond.
senses.whyCN: 此处 correlation 意为两组趋于匹配或对应。

senses.title: An act of correlating
senses.definition: the act of establishing a relationship between things
senses.definitionCN: 在事物之间建立关系的行为
senses.example: The correlation of the two data sets took weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 把两组数据关联起来花了数周。
senses.why: Correlation can name the act of finding the relationship, not just the relationship itself.
senses.whyCN: correlation 可以命名发现关系的行为，而不仅是关系本身。

senses.title: A reciprocal or complementary link
senses.definition: a reciprocal or complementary connection between things
senses.definitionCN: 事物之间互惠或互补的联系
senses.example: There is a correlation between supply and demand.
senses.exampleCN: 供需之间存在互补联系。
senses.why: When two things balance or complete each other, they show correlation.
senses.whyCN: 当两事物平衡或互补时，它们表现出 correlation。

senses.title: A pattern of co-occurrence
senses.definition: a pattern in which two things tend to appear or happen together
senses.definitionCN: 两事物倾向于一起出现或发生的模式
senses.example: Researchers noted a correlation between poverty and crime.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员注意到贫困与犯罪之间存在共现模式。
senses.why: Correlation can simply mean 'these things tend to go together', without claiming why.
senses.whyCN: correlation 可以仅表示「这些事物倾向于一起出现」，不声称原因。

senses.title: In grammar, a paired relationship
senses.definition: in grammar, a relationship between two words or clauses that work together
senses.definitionCN: 语法中，两个词或从句协同工作的关系
senses.example: 'Either...or' is a correlative conjunction.
senses.exampleCN: either...or 是关联连词。
senses.why: In grammar, correlatives are paired elements that depend on each other.
senses.whyCN: 在语法中，correlatives 是相互依赖的配对成分。

intro.en: Correlation is cor- (com-) + relation. Relation comes from Latin relatio, from referre 'to carry back'. The core is two things having a relation together.
intro.cn: correlation 是 cor-（com-）+ relation。relation 来自拉丁 relatio，relatio 源自 referre「带回」。核心是两事物一起具有关系。

items.en: ferre meant 'to carry'. referre is re- 'back' + ferre, meaning 'to carry back, relate'.
items.cn: ferre 意为「携带」。referre 是 re-「回」+ ferre，意为「带回、联系」。

items.en: relatio meant 'a bringing back, a relation, a report'.
items.cn: relatio 意为「带回、关系、报告」。

items.en: cor- is a form of com- 'together' used before r. correlation is 'a relation together'.
items.cn: cor- 是 com-「一起」在 r 前的形式。correlation 是「一起的关系」。

items.en: correlation = cor- + relation, formed in English or from Late Latin correlatio.
items.cn: correlation = cor- + relation，在英语中构成或来自后期拉丁 correlatio。

items.en: Correlation entered English in the 16th century, originally meaning 'a mutual relation'.
items.cn: correlation 在 16 世纪进入英语，最初意为「相互关系」。

items.en: The statistical sense developed in the 19th century with the work of Galton and Pearson.
items.cn: 统计义发展于 19 世纪，得益于高尔顿和皮尔逊的工作。

note.en: The first group shares ferre; the second contains near-synonyms for connection.
note.cn: 第一组共享 ferre；第二组是联系的近义词。

entries.definition: to have a mutual relationship; the verb behind correlation
entries.definitionCN: 具有相互关系；correlation 背后的动词

entries.definition: a connection between things; from relatio
entries.definitionCN: 事物之间的联系；来自 relatio

entries.definition: considered in relation to something else; from relatio
entries.definitionCN: 相对的；来自 relatio

entries.definition: a relationship between things; broader than correlation
entries.definitionCN: 事物之间的关系；比 correlation 更广

entries.definition: a connection between ideas or things; close to correlation
entries.definitionCN: 观念或事物之间的联系；接近 correlation

entries.definition: the way things are connected; broader than correlation
entries.definitionCN: 事物联系方式；比 correlation 更广

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real word relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分和真实同族词。

normal.en: cor- 'together' + relation: correlation is a relation two things have together.
normal.cn: cor-「一起」+ relation：correlation 是两事物一起具有的关系。

normal.en: correlate is the verb; correlation is the noun of the relationship.
normal.cn: correlate 是动词；correlation 是关系的名词。

normal.en: Correlation does not imply causation: things can vary together without one causing the other.
normal.cn: 相关不意味着因果：事物可以一起变化而无因果关系。

normal.en: A positive correlation means both go up together; negative means one up, one down.
normal.cn: 正相关意味着两者同升；负相关意味着一升一降。

normal.en: relation is the base; correlation adds cor- to emphasize the mutual link.
normal.cn: relation 是基础；correlation 加 cor- 强调相互联系。

abstract.en: Think of two dancers moving in sync: their movements show correlation.
abstract.cn: 想象两个舞者同步移动：他们的动作显示出 correlation。

abstract.en: Think of two lines on a graph that rise and fall together: that is correlation.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上两条同升同降的线：那就是 correlation。

abstract.en: Think of 'co-' meaning together: correlation = relation together.
abstract.cn: 把 co- 想成「一起」：correlation = 一起的关系。

examples.en: Scientists found a correlation between sleep and productivity.
examples.cn: 科学家发现睡眠与生产力之间存在关联。

examples.en: The correlation coefficient was 0.8, indicating a strong relationship.
examples.cn: 相关系数为 0.8，表明存在强相关关系。

examples.en: There is a high correlation between education level and income.
examples.cn: 教育水平与收入之间存在高度相关。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「靠瑞雷神」——靠（cor-）着关系（relation）一起走 → correlation 关联

root: 拉丁 referre「带回、联系」（re-「回」+ ferre「携带」）→ relatio「关系」+ cor-（com-「一起」）→ correlation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all mean 'a relation two things share': statistical, causal, matching, or grammatical.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都表示「两事物共享的关系」：统计的、因果的、匹配的或语法的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two lines on a graph rising and falling together.
core.cn: 核心意象：图表上两条同升同降的线。

branches.en: GENERAL RELATIONSHIP: a connection between things.
branches.cn: 一般关系：事物之间的联系。

branches.en: STATISTICAL CORRELATION: a quantified measure of co-variation.
branches.cn: 统计相关：共变的量化度量。

branches.en: MATCHING OR COMPLEMENTARY: sets or forces that correspond.
branches.cn: 匹配或互补：相对应的集合或力量。

branches.en: ACT OF CORRELATING: the process of linking things.
branches.cn: 关联行为：把事物联系起来的过程。

branches.en: CO-OCCURRENCE OR GRAMMAR: things that appear together or pair up.
branches.cn: 共现或语法：一起出现或配对的事物。

intro.en: Correlation is cor- (com-) + relation. The prefix cor- is fossilized; relation comes from Latin relatio (referre).
intro.cn: correlation 是 cor-（com-）+ relation。前缀 cor- 已凝固；relation 来自拉丁 relatio（referre）。

latinIntro.en: Latin ferre 'to carry' produced refer, relate, relation, transfer, defer, infer, offer. Root: fer-/lat-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ferre「携带」产生了 refer、relate、relation、transfer、defer、infer、offer。词根：fer-/lat-。
